acceptance_criteria.criterion: RepositoryRegistrySchema accepts a valid .repositories.json object with one or more repository entries, each having id, label, folder_names, vision, created_at, and last_modified.
RepositoryEntrySchema rejects entries where id does not match SLUG_REGEX.
StrategicVisionSchema accepts all three fields as null (vision not yet authored) and as non-empty strings.
All schemas export corresponding TypeScript types.

summary: Created mcp-server/src/schema/repository-registry.ts with StrategicVisionSchema, RepositoryEntrySchema, and RepositoryRegistrySchema using the SLUG_REGEX from knowledge.ts as the single source of truth for id validation.

Created mcp-server/tests/schema/repository-registry.test.ts with 40 tests covering: valid/null/mixed vision fields, empty string rejection, SLUG_REGEX acceptance and rejection cases, required field presence, empty registry, multi-entry registry, and type export compile-time checks.
All 40 new tests pass; full suite of 2934 tests passes with no regressions.

comments.note: SLUG_REGEX is re-used from knowledge.ts (the single source of truth) rather than duplicated — clean and consistent with the project pattern documented in that file's JSDoc.

StrategicVisionSchema rejects empty strings (min(1)) to prevent 'blank' vision values that are visually indistinguishable from null in the GUI — this is a small but meaningful UX guard, documented in the schema JSDoc.

mcp-server/src/schema/repository-registry.ts does not export a SLUG_REGEX re-export; consumers must import it from knowledge.ts. If future WPs add additional slug-validated fields in this file, a local re-export (e.g. `export { SLUG_REGEX } from './knowledge.js'`) would improve discoverability without duplication.

comments.note: StrategicVisionSchema correctly rejects empty strings (min(1)) — prevents blank-but-non-null vision values reaching the GUI, consistent with the JSDoc comment.

This is intentional (uniqueness should be enforced at the storage layer in WP-003), but the Reviewer and Developer should confirm that the storage module validates this before writing.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/src/schema/repository-registry.ts and mcp-server/tests/schema/repository-registry.test.ts against all four review dimensions.
No blocking issues found. Schema is clean, well-composed, and architecturally sound.
StrategicVisionSchema → RepositoryEntrySchema → RepositoryRegistrySchema composes correctly bottom-up.
SLUG_REGEX is re-used from knowledge.ts (single source of truth) — no duplication.
Timestamp fields (created_at, last_modified) use z.string() with no format constraint, consistent with the project-wide convention established in knowledge.ts.
id uniqueness is intentionally deferred to the storage layer — correct separation of concerns; no schema-layer action required for this WP.
40 unit tests provide strong coverage; type-export compile-time checks are a good pattern.
No Fix-Forward edits applied. One Documentation-Forward item recorded for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: Schema composition (StrategicVisionSchema → RepositoryEntrySchema → RepositoryRegistrySchema) is clean and follows the principle of least surprise. Each schema is independently usable, which is good for future composability.

The JSDoc comment on RepositoryEntrySchema.id explicitly calls out the path-traversal safety property of SLUG_REGEX. This is valuable institutional knowledge — future contributors will understand why the regex is there, not just what it does.
The empty-string rejection on StrategicVisionSchema (min(1)) is a good defensive pattern for nullable fields. The rationale is documented inline, which makes it a non-surprising constraint.

[documentation-forward] created_at and last_modified on RepositoryEntrySchema use z.string() with no ISO 8601 format constraint — consistent with the project convention in knowledge.ts (which does the same). The JSDoc mentions 'ISO 8601 timestamp' but the schema itself does not enforce this. The Documentation agent should add a note in the schema-level JSDoc or a module-level comment clarifying that ISO 8601 format is expected by convention and enforced by the storage layer, not by the Zod schema — consistent with the pattern in knowledge.ts InsightSchema.created_at.
